whys.compose.default: The mist is bright and busy, so a soft darkened halo behind the letters and the sandwich that keeps the kayak in front guarantee the type reads without covering the subject.
whys.idea: The footage is a single continuous kayak drift through mist, so putting the words behind the subject keeps the subject solid and lets the mist carry the type; the 90bpm slow blues and the two chord changes give exactly three colour moments for the four words.
whys.system: The four words are short and the shots are calm, so a single behind-the-subject system with one expressive face per word and a chord-locked colour step is the cleanest way to keep the piece readable and musical without adding a second motion on top of the footage.
whys.word[0] WAKE: Opens the piece on the first downbeat at 1.34s; a playful 3D face matches the bright red kayak and the slow blues groove, and the lanes module reads cleanly on the calm water behind the subject.
whys.word[1] DRIFT: Lands exactly on the 4s chord change; the ornamental Codystar face is characterful for the longest word, and the footage already forms DRIFT as glowing wire strands so a handoff to glowing tubes keeps the word part of the world.
whys.word[2] TURN: Hits the 6.67s chord change as the kayak carves its arc; the broken inline Monofett face suits the turn, and the short word stays legible behind the subject.
whys.word[3] BREATHE: The longest word gets the longest hold into the 14.88s dropout; the playful inline Bungee face and a slow wipe form suit the final stillness as the kayak glides away at sunrise.
